newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says some aid to Opel Spain was illegal.
newsitem.headline: EU says some aid to Opel Spain was illegal.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it did not approve 200 million pesetas ($1.6 million) in aid, most of which has been paid to Opel Spain, a wholly owned subsidiary of General Motors (GM).

The Commission said in a statement that its analysis and that of an independent expert of the aid, given towards the total cost of some 1.3 billion pesetas for the development of software, was not compatible with European Union state aid rules.
It said the Spanish government had undertaken to recover 161 million pesetas already paid to the Saragossa-based firm.

In the same decision, the Commission gave retroactive approval of another grant of 100 million pesetas to help introduce new technology at the plant in 1994 and a 68-million peseta subsidy for the vocational training of 500 employees who were involved in using the new technology.
The Spanish subsidiary of GM, which produces Opel Corsas and Astras, had a turnover of 465 billion pesetas in 1993 and net profits of 19 billion pesetas, the EU said.
